lines.text: Your agents write essays. You’re on a train.
Seven lines. Each one a decision.
On glasses today, you can approve, or say one sentence.
A yes or no doesn’t steer an agent.
When a thread needs you, it finds your phone.
Your glasses mirror it.
One thread. A seven-step plan.
Every point is one line, tied to the plan’s own words.
Step four would sign everyone out.
Tap. Talk.
Your objection lands on that exact step.
Step six: a mutex that deadlocks with the retry path.
The rest pass in silence.
Preview. One tap to send.
Sent to the agent.
Back to the train.
It lands in the thread as a cited review.
The agent revises the plan and keeps working.
Laptop-quality feedback. From your glasses.
Questions come as options.
One tap: stay on six for now.
Four drafts from your inbox agent.
Three pass in silence.
One correction: Thursday, not Tuesday.
Cleared in twenty-five seconds.
The full plan waits in a Telegram topic.
Every note is a quote-reply on its exact sentence.
Read on phone, right where you stopped.
Ring for where. Voice for what.
Even G2, R1, T3 Code, Telegram. Open source.
